findings.description: The release workflow pipes the GPG private key secret into gpg via echo, which risks exposing the secret in workflow logs if command tracing or error output is enabled.
findings.remediation: Avoid echoing secrets; import the key from a file written with a masked step, or use a dedicated action that reads the secret without printing it, and ensure `set -x` is never active around secret handling.

findings.description: GitHub Actions are referenced by mutable version tags (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-go@v5, actions/upload-artifact@v4, softprops/action-gh-release@v1) rather than pinned commit SHAs, exposing the release pipeline to supply-chain attacks if a tag is moved.
findings.remediation: Pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA (e.g. actions/checkout@<sha>) and let Dependabot update the pins.

evidence.snippet: uses: actions/checkout@v4 / uses: actions/setup-go@v5 / uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v1

findings.description: None of the qa, build, or release jobs define timeout-minutes, so a hung test, build, or gpg step can occupy a runner indefinitely.
findings.remediation: Add `timeout-minutes` (e.g. 15 for qa, 30 for build/release) to each job definition.

evidence.snippet:
jobs:
  qa:
    name: Quality Assurance
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

findings.description: The workflow does not declare a top-level `permissions:` block, so jobs inherit the repository default token permissions, which may be read-write for all scopes.
findings.remediation: Add a top-level `permissions: contents: read` and grant `contents: write` only to the release job that needs it.

findings.description: The release job runs automatically on any pushed v*.*.* tag and publishes a GitHub release with signed artifacts and no manual approval gate or environment protection.
findings.remediation: Gate the release job behind a protected GitHub Environment requiring manual approval, or require a signed tag verified before publishing.

evidence.metric: release triggered directly by tag push

findings.description: The Prometheus exporter server is started with `go srv.ListenAndServe()` and its returned error is discarded, so a bind failure (e.g. port already in use) is silently ignored and the exporter never runs.
findings.remediation: Capture the error from ListenAndServe and surface it, e.g. `go func() { if err := srv.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed { log.Printf(...) } }()`.

findings.description: In encode(), the multiCloser returned by decoder() is deferred before its error is checked, so when decoder() fails the deferred mc.Close() runs on a partially constructed closer and the returned error is inspected only after the defer is registered.
findings.remediation: Check the error from decoder() before registering the defer, or restructure so `defer mc.Close()` is only registered after `err == nil`.

findings.description: The error returned by the Prometheus HTTP server goroutine is never observed, so operators receive no signal when the metrics endpoint fails to start.
findings.remediation: Route the ListenAndServe error into the attack error path or log it with the configured logger so failures are visible.

findings.description: The qa and build jobs run `actions/setup-go@v5` without enabling the built-in module cache (`cache: true`), so Go modules are re-downloaded on every run, wasting CI minutes.
findings.remediation: Set `cache: true` (or `cache-dependency-path: go.sum`) on the setup-go steps to reuse the module cache across runs.

evidence.metric: no cache configured on 2 setup-go steps

findings.description: The build matrix expands to 14 OS/arch combinations on every tagged release, including rarely used targets (freebsd/386, openbsd/arm64, windows/386), multiplying runner minutes for each release.
findings.remediation: Trim the matrix to actively supported targets or split rarely used targets into a separate, manually triggered workflow.
